name: Duplicate-Contact & Data-Hygiene Watchdog

parameters.content:
## Duplicate-Contact & Data-Hygiene Watchdog

### How it works

1. The workflow runs daily to scan Clio contacts for potential duplicates.
2. It fetches all contacts from Clio and scores pairs for duplicate likelihood.
3. It filters and reports new high-confidence duplicate pairs via a digest email.
4. The workflow logs the scan results to an audit and notifies a paralegal via email.
5. It also handles dismissal of flagged pairs through a webhook, recording dismissals and confirming to the user.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Configure the Clio API credentials and set the environment variable CLIO_BASE_URL.
- [ ] Provide email sending credentials for the notification node.
- [ ] Deploy and configure the webhook URL accessible for dismissal link clicks.
- [ ] Ensure the sub-workflow for logging duplicate scans is available and configured.

### Customization

You can adjust the confidence threshold in the "Filter To New High-Confidence Pairs" node's code to tune sensitivity. Customizing the email content in the "Build Duplicate Contact Alert Email" node allows for tailored notifications. The schedule trigger can be modified to change the scan frequency.

## Duplicate scan trigger and fetch

Starts with the daily schedule trigger and fetches all Clio contacts to begin the duplicate scanning process.

## Duplicate detection and filtering

Scores pairs for duplicates, then conditionally filters to new high-confidence pairs or skips if none found.

## Duplicate reporting decision

Checks if there are new pairs to report, builds the alert email, or skips if no new pairs are found.

## Logging and notification

Logs the duplicate scan result to an audit sub-workflow and sends a notification email to the paralegal.

## Dismissal webhook and confirmation

Handles dismissal webhook trigger, records the dismissal, and shows a confirmation page.

nodes.name: Every Morning at 6am
nodes.notes:
Runs the duplicate scan once a day at 6am (n8n server timezone). Change the cron expression to run more or less often — a weekly scan (e.g. '0 6 * * 1' for Monday mornings) is plenty for most solo/small firms; daily suits firms adding many new contacts.

This is the only thing that starts a scan — nothing else in this workflow runs unless this fires or a paralegal clicks a Dismiss link.

nodes.name: Fetch All Clio Contacts
nodes.notes:
Pulls every contact from Clio for today's scan.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search 'OAuth2 API' → Grant Type: Authorization Code → Authorization URL: '{CLIO_BASE_URL}/oauth/authorize' → Access Token URL: '{CLIO_BASE_URL}/oauth/token' → Client ID/Secret from your Clio Developer Application → Authentication: Body (Clio expects client_id/client_secret in the token-exchange body, not a Basic Auth header) → save as 'Clio API (OAuth2)', then click Connect my account.

Clio access tokens expire after 30 days — OAuth2 API handles refreshing automatically via the refresh token, unlike a static Header Auth Bearer token which silently goes stale and has to be replaced by hand.

limit=200 covers typical solo/small firm contact volumes in a single request. If your firm has more than 200 contacts, raise this value; this node does not paginate beyond one request.

CLIO_BASE_URL is shared with every other Clio-integrated template in this catalog (e.g. https://app.clio.com or https://eu.app.clio.com) — set once in Variables, reused everywhere.

nodes.name: Score Likely Duplicate Contact Pairs
nodes.notes:
Compares every contact against every other contact of the same type (Person vs Person, Company vs Company — never cross-type) and scores duplicate likelihood 0-100.

Scoring: exact email match and exact phone match each contribute 50 points, fuzzy name similarity contributes up to 30 points (Levenshtein edit distance, so 'Jon Smith' and 'John Smith' score highly even without an exact match). Either exact match alone plus a reasonably similar name clears the default 70-point threshold; name similarity alone never does. Pairs scoring below 40 are dropped immediately as noise.

Output: a single item with the full pairs array, pair_count, and has_pairs — not one item per pair. The next gate checks has_pairs before anything is split out further.

nodes.name: If Duplicate Pairs Found
nodes.notes:
Yes (at least one pair scored 40+) → continue to the threshold/dedupe filter.
No (zero candidate pairs, or zero/one contacts total) → route to Skip. A quiet day is the expected common case for a healthy contact list.

nodes.name: Skip No Duplicate Pairs Found
nodes.notes: No candidate pairs scored above the 40-point noise floor this run. No email sent. Visible in execution history to confirm the scan actually ran.

nodes.name: Filter New High-Confidence Pairs
nodes.notes:
Applies DUPLICATE_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD (n8n Variable, defaults to 70 if unset) and drops any pair already seen — flagged in a previous run or dismissed by a paralegal.

Uses global-scope static data specifically because the Dismiss webhook path (a separate node, separate trigger) needs to write to the same seenPairs map that this node reads and writes — node-scoped static data would give each node its own isolated store and the dedupe would silently stop working.

Entries older than 90 days are pruned automatically so this never grows unbounded.

nodes.name: If New Duplicate Pairs To Report
nodes.notes:
Yes (at least one pair is new and above threshold) → build and send the digest email.
No (everything today was below threshold, or already flagged/dismissed previously) → route to Skip. No email sent — the paralegal isn't re-alerted about pairs they've already seen.

nodes.name: Skip No New Pairs To Report
nodes.notes: Every candidate pair today was either below the confidence threshold or already flagged/dismissed in a previous run. No email sent.

nodes.name: Build Duplicate Contact Alert Email
nodes.notes:
Builds the full digest email — every newly-flagged pair, why it matched, direct links to both Clio contact records, and a one-click Dismiss link per pair.

Variables read (project → Variables tab):
  FIRM_NAME, FIRM_FROM_EMAIL — as used across this catalog
  FIRM_PARALEGAL_EMAIL — who receives this digest; falls back to FIRM_EMAIL if unset
  CLIO_BASE_URL — shared with PAC-18/PAC-20, used to build the '/nc/#/contacts/{id}' deep link
  DUPLICATE_DISMISS_WEBHOOK_URL — the Production URL of 'When Dismiss Link Clicked' below; must be set manually after first activating this workflow, since n8n can't self-reference another node's production URL across trigger paths

nodes.name: Log Scan To Compliance Audit
nodes.notes:
Calls the Bar-Compliance Guardrail to log this scan to your compliance audit sheet.

This workflow alerts your own paralegal, not a client — so opt-out checking does not apply and approved will always be true here. The purpose of this call is the audit trail: how many pairs were flagged and when.

The guardrail workflow ID is read from the GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID n8n Variable (Settings → Variables). Set it to the numeric ID from the Bar-Compliance Guardrail workflow URL: .../workflow/WORKFLOW_ID.

value.message: ={{ $json.new_pair_count }} possible duplicate contact pair(s) flagged in Clio and emailed to the paralegal.

nodes.name: Send Duplicate Alert Email
nodes.notes:
Delivers the digest to your paralegal (or firm email if no dedicated paralegal address is configured).

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → enter your email provider's settings → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.

All values are read from 'Build Duplicate Contact Alert Email' — not the immediate input — because the guardrail's response has a different data shape than the digest content.

nodes.name: When Dismiss Link Clicked
nodes.notes:
Receives the click when a paralegal opens the 'Dismiss' link from the alert email — a plain GET request with a pair_id query parameter, safe to click straight from an email client or browser (no form, no POST).

After first activating this workflow, copy this node's Production URL and set it as the DUPLICATE_DISMISS_WEBHOOK_URL n8n Variable so 'Build Duplicate Contact Alert Email' can construct working Dismiss links.

responseMode is set to 'responseNode' so the confirmation page comes from the 'Show Dismissal Confirmation Page' node below, rather than n8n's default immediate empty response.

nodes.name: Record Duplicate Dismissal
nodes.notes:
Writes the dismissal into the shared seenPairs static data so 'Filter To New High-Confidence Pairs' skips this pair in every future scan, and builds a short confirmation page.

No authentication on this link by design — it's meant to be one click from an email client. The only action it can take is suppressing a specific pair_id from future reports; it cannot modify or delete anything in Clio.

nodes.name: Show Dismissal Confirmation Page
nodes.notes: Returns the confirmation page to whatever browser the paralegal clicked the Dismiss link from. Plain HTML, no styling dependencies — safe to render in any mail client's in-app browser.

main.node: If New Duplicate Pairs To Report
Skip No New Pairs To Report

description: Runs a scheduled fuzzy-match pass over Clio contacts, scores every pair for duplicate likelihood (exact email/phone match plus Levenshtein name similarity), and emails a digest to the paralegal — each pair, why it matched, a direct link to view both contacts in Clio, and a one-click Dismiss link. Clio has no merge feature (not in the app, not via API), so merging stays a manual step in Clio; this template only finds and flags. Dedupes flagged/dismissed pairs with n8n's built-in static data, no external database. Replaces manual CRM cleanup and Insycle/Cloudingo-style dedupe tools. Logs every scan to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet.
